races.name: Nora Canty Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bethpage Theatre
runners_data.note: Fell on debut but breeding suggests ability, prominent runner who could benefit from race experience over this ideal trip
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to useful 2m1f-2m6f hurdle/chase winner Drumgill; 100-1 for debut at Cork, fell halfway.

runners_data.name: Kauto Empress
runners_data.note: Debutante with outstanding Kauto Star family connections, unknown quantity but breeding screams class
runners_data.spotlight: Robin Of Navan 5yo; dam unraced sister to French 2m hurdle/2m1f chase winner Kauto Sirtaki, out of maiden sister to outstanding chaser Kauto Star.

runners_data.name: Misty Valentine
runners_data.note: Second Winters newcomer with solid pointing family, 4-year-old receives weight allowance
runners_data.spotlight: Second newcomer for yard; half-sister to winners Handmedownastar (point/2m3f hurdle) and Aleish Lass (point/2m6f hurdle); dam unraced sister to point winner Shalltoo, half-sister to smart 2m4f-3m hurdle/chase winner Dedigout, out of bumper winner.

runners_data.name: Salsinha
runners_data.note: Proven class act in prominent style, De Bromhead 28% strike-rate this season gives confidence in placement
runners_data.spotlight: Won good-ground bumper on last summer's debut; good level of form in four starts over hurdles; third in Listed contest at Thurles before Christmas; fourth when odds-on at Fairyhouse in April; little wrong with her second to 122-rated foe at Punchestown; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Tumbling In
runners_data.note: Sister to high-class Dream On Baby returns after 226-day break, prominent type who needs this run
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to 134-rated hurdler Dream On Baby showed potential in two bumpers in early autumn; will come for this, but not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Poetisa
runners_data.note: Mullins front-runner disappointed at odds-on last time, needs to settle better to use Cheltenham bumper form
runners_data.spotlight: Cost plenty after winning a good-ground bumper at Cheltenham last April; turned over at 4-7 on stable/hurdling debut in January; reversed form with the winner when second to highly talented Zanoosh in Listed contest at Navan (2m4f, heavy); returned to bumpers then, second to useful mare at Naas, beaten a long way against geldings last time.

runners_data.name: Pure Logic
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with headgear applied, solid each-way claims despite moderate rating
runners_data.spotlight: Second in three bumpers and a Ballinrobe maiden hurdle; well held on return at Killarney; headgear.

runners_data.name: Hillhead Runner
runners_data.note: Front-runner with bumper win on CV, stable debut suggests acclimatisation needed after yard switch
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner for Peter Fahey and placed three times in summer maiden hurdles last year for Gavin Cromwell; after a long layoff, well beaten on stable debut at Cork.

runners_data.name: Wonderful Everyday
runners_data.note: Mullins hold-up type who won mares bumper, Paul Townend booking significant for this yard
runners_data.spotlight: Did well to beat the geldings on debut in last year's Goffs Defender Bumper at Punchestown; has contested black-type bumpers since, well beaten three times but second in Listed contest at Fairyhouse two runs back; closely related to 2m3f hurdle winner and Townend's choice over the more experienced Poetisa.

runners_data.name: Rose Mountain
runners_data.note: Returns after 455-day absence having been well beaten in both bumpers, needs major improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Big prices and well held in two bumpers.

runners_data.name: Shanliss Tricks
runners_data.note: Beaten 54 lengths in both hurdle starts, hood applied but hard to fancy on exposed form
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 54l in both hurdle starts.

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Bumper winner who disappointed badly over hurdles, prominent style but confidence questionable
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner last summer but tailed off in both hurdle outings.

runners_data.name: Colugo
runners_data.note: Flat maiden making hurdles debut, hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario despite modest ability
runners_data.spotlight: Modest maiden on the level; keen-goer needs this run to get a handicap mark.

runners_data.name: The Fog Horn
runners_data.note: Dual 7f winner stepping up to hurdles, prominent type but form suggests out of depth at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 7f winner; huge prices and well beaten in two hurdle runs.

races.paceDynamic: Poetisa and Hillhead Runner will contest the early lead with both confirmed front-runners, creating an honest gallop from the outset. The midfield will be congested with Salsinha, Pure Logic, Fraher Field, and The Fog Horn all wanting prominent positions, creating traffic problems approaching the business end. Wonderful Everyday and Colugo will track from off the pace as the only genuine hold-up horses in the field. This strong early pace and prominent congestion clearly favours the patient hold-up performers who can avoid the early scrimmaging and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuine between Poetisa and Hillhead Runner
scenarios.body: The prominent pack gets into trouble 2-3 out while the patient runners get clear runs to exploit tired leaders. Wonderful Everyday and Colugo benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent perseveres
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners gets the jump on the field turning in
scenarios.body: Salsinha or Pure Logic times their move perfectly to slip the pack and holds off late challengers. The De Bromhead/Hanlon experience proves crucial in a tactical finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner stays
scenarios.trigger: If Poetisa settles better than expected and gets an easy lead
scenarios.body: She repeats her Cheltenham bumper win by dictating terms and proving too classy for this maiden company. Hillhead Runner might also benefit if getting first run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the Winters debutantes shows untapped ability
scenarios.body: Kauto Empress or Misty Valentine benefits from race experience while others compromise each other. The breeding suggests genuine ability waiting to be unlocked.

watchPoints.text: Traffic problems developing 2-3 out with Salsinha, Pure Logic, Fraher Field and The Fog Horn all wanting the same prominent positions
Poetisa's settling ability after disappointing when odds-on favourite on stable debut in January
Paul Townend's booking of Wonderful Everyday suggests Mullins expects improvement from mares bumper winner
Both Winters debutantes Kauto Empress and Misty Valentine carry strong breeding but are complete unknowns
Hillhead Runner's adaptation to new yard after disappointing stable debut following long layoff

races.name: Southern Waste Management Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with recent improvement over hurdles who should get an uncontested lead
runners_data.spotlight: Latest of three Flat wins for Jessica Harrington was off 84 last summer; improved of late over hurdles; mild promise when sixth at Bellewstown and then 22-1, dropped in grade to beat geldings at Wexford; needs proper good ground and trainer admits she's unpredictable.

runners_data.name: Diamond Tipp
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 57-day break but has proven form on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Won good-ground 2m2f maiden at Downpatrick last July and some okay runs at same track after; pulled up on testing ground on first run of the year at Fairyhouse and has since left John McConnell.

runners_data.name: Shannon Bank
runners_data.note: Handy racer making stable debut for Andrew Kinirons after decent Killarney second
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in two bumpers for Seamus Fahey and second in 2m1f Killarney handicap hurdle in October when with Gavin Cromwell; unfancied on stable debut, and first run of the year, when mid-field in Wexford chase; might prefer farther, but not out of it.

runners_data.name: Patty O'Farrell
runners_data.note: Previous course winner dropped 4lbs but hasn't threatened since on softer ground
runners_data.spotlight: Having finished second at Naas in April, won this off 4lb lower last year and was third at Roscommon next time; hasn't threatened since on softer terrain but decent ground is key to her and she might bounce back to form; usual rider has jumped ship to Shannon Bank, but sub isn't too shabby.

runners_data.name: Cool Summer
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with top rider Darragh O'Keeffe but quiet since seasonal reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Some useful bumper form and was third in Roscommon maiden on hurdling debut; quiet since, including on first run of the year at Tramore in April, but has top rider on board for the first time on this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 190-day absence but has winning form on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Won three handicaps for previous yard and likes good ground; 1m6f Flat winner last year when her hurdles form wasn't great; has dropped down to last winning mark, but not a hectic record when fresh and last two wins have come in cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Mollys Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with hood after improved run last time following keen tendencies
runners_data.spotlight: Keen-goer was sixth in a good bumper at Cork in March (winner and third won next time); fitted with a hood, still looked a tricky ride but ran much better on third hurdles start last month, keeping on when beaten 12l in decent maiden at Down Royal; handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who found form for new yard last summer but beaten easily at festival
runners_data.spotlight: Long-standing maiden until joining yard last summer and then went back-to-back at Wexford in July/August; well beaten at the festival here on next start and has struggled since; better ground will help and she's 1lb lower than last winning mark.

runners_data.name: Western Princess
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse described as difficult ride with only 6 days since last run
runners_data.spotlight: Remote third at Wexford her best finishing position; can be keen and described as 'a very difficult ride' when connections were called in by the stewards after she was fifth at Ballinrobe; after a year's absence, ran in the corresponding race at Ballinrobe last week, keen again and had weakened out of it when falling at the last; readily opposed on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making handicap debut but has been beaten miles in maiden company
runners_data.spotlight: Okay bumper run on debut but has been beaten miles in her maiden outings; handicap debut for well-related 5yo.

races.paceDynamic: Mo Ghille Mar will set a controlled tempo from the front with Diamond Tipp and Shannon Bank tracking closely in the prominent positions. The pace will be sustainable rather than fierce given the lack of natural speed horses, allowing the field to remain competitive deep into the race. This tempo will suit horses who can travel well in the first half before quickening, rather than pure front-runners or hold-up horses who need a strong pace to aim at. The tactical verdict clearly favours prominent racers who can position handy and have the stamina to sustain their effort over this 2m trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Favours Class
scenarios.trigger: If Mo Ghille Mar sets an uncontested lead and the pace stays manageable throughout
scenarios.body: The higher-rated horses can use their superior ability to outstay the field in a tactical finish. Diamond Tipp and Mo Ghille Mar can dictate terms and prove too classy for the remainder.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pressure Creates Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Shannon Bank or Diamond Tipp press Mo Ghille Mar from the start creating genuine pace
scenarios.body: The front-runners tie up in the final furlong allowing late-closing horses to sweep past. Inchiquin Star and Chosen Shant benefit from the strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays slow throughout and becomes a sprint from the last hurdle
scenarios.body: Horses with high cruising speed rather than stamina dominate the finish. Mollys Star and Cool Summer can quicken best when the race becomes tactical.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Mo Ghille Mar goes too slow and no one wants to commit early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a crawl that turns into a sprint where class tells. The highest-rated horses Mo Ghille Mar and Diamond Tipp simply outclass weaker rivals in a slow-run race.

watchPoints.text: Western Princess could cause interference as she's described as a very difficult ride and keen-going
Mo Ghille Mar might go too slow up front if no one pressures him early creating tactical complications
Diamond Tipp returning after 57 days but has shown best form on good ground conditions
Inchiquin Star makes first appearance in 190 days which could blunt her finishing kick
Mollys Star fitted with hood suggesting ongoing temperament issues that could resurface under pressure

races.name: Join Racing TV With A Free Trial Now Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Becasse
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 23-day break with Henry De Bromhead's 11/39 14-day record, likely to control early tempo
runners_data.spotlight: French hurdle winner on very soft in October 2024; back from an absence to finish second in a Wexford handicap (soft) and departed too far out to tell what might have happened when 6-1 at Killarney; remains unexposed.

runners_data.name: Wholelotofbusiness
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the tactical setup, Eoin McCarthy's 2/13 record modest but horse shows consistent form on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Won a novice at Killarney in October (2m1f, yielding) and probably posted a similar effort when third in a handicap there last month; solid chance off an untouched mark.

runners_data.name: Fast Felix
runners_data.note: Forward-going type who finished alongside stablemate Wholelotofbusiness last time, 7lb claimer Thomas O'Connor takes useful weight off
runners_data.spotlight: Lost his way in the winter but refreshed from a break he was a pleasing fourth at Killarney, finishing upsides shorter-priced stablemate Wholelotofbusiness; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Icare Desbois
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but regressive form suggests limited winning chances despite David Kelly's decent 3/6 strike rate
runners_data.spotlight: Former Willie Mullins inmate; now looks regressive and was behind some of these at Killarney three weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Cappucino
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose current wellbeing questioned after mixed chase form, 25 days since last run could help freshness
runners_data.spotlight: Won his bumper here and added a Punchestown maiden hurdle; he's been good and bad in six defeats over fences and current wellbeing is a bit of an issue ahead of this return to hurdling.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar
runners_data.note: Patient type returning from 34-day Flat run, previous Listed hurdle form suggests class edge if pace setup suits
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to fire on the Flat last time but had previously returned to hurdles (dual winner) with a respectable fifth of 21 in a Listed handicap at Punchestown (2m, yielding); off the same mark here in a less demanding race.

runners_data.name: Frankendael
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer lightly campaigned since September Listed win here, 5lb claimer Patrick O'Brien reduces weight burden significantly
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced since winning a Listed handicap here in September 2024; back from an absence, he was a much bigger price than Putapoundinthejar at Punchestown in April and duly finished well behind the Martin horse.

runners_data.name: Spy
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse returning from month break, may need the run after lengthy previous absence affected Punchestown effort
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose gelding who is consistent in the main and he was returning from a lengthy break when never that competitive at Punchestown a month ago; perhaps a shade high in the weights, even if he can return to best.

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Back marker who showed revival at Wexford, 6-year-old maiden winner gets significant weight relief but faces class rise
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden winner who appeared to be going nowhere until a revived second of 14 at Wexford (2m1f, good to yielding); nudged up 2lb for that but a greater worry would be that this is a better race.

races.paceDynamic: Becasse looks the only confirmed front runner in this field, with Wholelotofbusiness, Fast Felix and Icare Desbois likely to track prominently but none showing strong pace-forcing tendencies. This sets up a moderate early gallop that should build steadily through the race rather than creating a searching test from the outset. The majority of the field including Putapoundinthejar, Frankendael, Spy, Cappucino and Bossing It will settle back and look to make late moves. This tactical setup clearly favours the prominent racers who can position close enough to strike when the pace lifts, as the hold-up horses may struggle to pick up the pieces if the pace proves only honest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Pays
scenarios.trigger: If Becasse sets honest fractions and the prominent trio apply gradual pressure from halfway
scenarios.body: Wholelotofbusiness and Fast Felix can utilise their tactical speed to strike in the final furlong when the pace builds. The hold-up horses get caught flat-footed by the change of tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays truly sedate throughout and becomes a sprint from the last hurdle
scenarios.body: Putapoundinthejar and Spy can unleash their finishing kicks to maximum effect in a slowly-run race. The prominent horses get swamped by the late charge having done too much.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Becasse Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If no horse challenges Becasse early and he dictates throughout unchallenged
scenarios.body: The leader can control the tempo completely and kick for home with enough left in reserve. The field gets strung out behind with no one able to mount a serious challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses engage Becasse early creating a strong gallop throughout
scenarios.body: All the early pace sets up perfectly for the patient hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders. Frankendael and Cappucino benefit from the honest tempo despite their back positions.

watchPoints.text: Becasse if allowed uncontested lead early - could dictate throughout and prove hard to peg back
Fast Felix and Wholelotofbusiness if tracking too close together - stablemates may compromise each other's chances
Putapoundinthejar for market confidence given trainer A J Martin's 2/9 record and horse's dual-purpose campaign
Frankendael's jumping fluency on return from 34-day break after trainer McNamara's 0/12 recent record
Overall pace development through first mile - genuine gallop essential for hold-up horses to be competitive

races.name: John B. Keane Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Tropical Image
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with crucial course-and-distance form advantage, returning to the scene of her only career win
runners_data.spotlight: Her sole career win came in a 2m6f handicap hurdle here in September; beaten 22l in a 2m4f handicap on her belated chase debut but it wasn't a bad run.

runners_data.name: Whispering Willow
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with strong recent chase form but needs genuine pace collapse to be effective from the rear
runners_data.spotlight: Much improved to make a successful stable debut in a 2m handicap hurdle at Punchestown and she nearly followed up on chase debut at Downpatrick (2m3f, good to yielding); jumped soundly enough that day and the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Walk Away Harry
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner showing regressive form with concerning fade pattern that makes stamina doubtful
runners_data.spotlight: His best hurdles form for Charles Byrnes seems long gone and he's now regressive; well beaten in his previous chase this January.

runners_data.name: Derby Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning from 291-day absence after poor chase debut, hard to trust on comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to raise his modest profile when tailed off on chase debut at Tramore (2m6f, good); hard to warm to on this return from an absence.

runners_data.name: Knockbrack Rambler
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with poor chase record and fade tendencies, testing conditions won't help
runners_data.comment: No closer than 20l in five defeats over fences and was pulled up back hurdling last time
runners_data.spotlight: No closer than 20l in five defeats over fences and was pulled up back hurdling last time; testing ground was no excuse as he enjoys the mud.

runners_data.name: Uptaurintop
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making quick return from poor chase debut 11 days ago, stamina questions persist
runners_data.spotlight: Close up in a 2m handicap hurdle at Limerick (soft to heavy; first-time tongue-tie) before finishing well behind on his chase debut back there 11 days ago when an early mistake didn't help his cause; could have a part to play if avoiding similar mishaps.

runners_data.name: Brave Endeavour
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who faded badly on chase debut but gets tactical advantage of uncontested lead
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who went 0-6 over hurdles; led early but ended up tailed off in a 2m4f Limerick handicap on recent chase debut; he does have some ability and this is a desperately weak race.

races.paceDynamic: Brave Endeavour is the sole confirmed front runner and will get an uncontested lead from the start. With most of the field preferring to sit back (Whispering Willow, Walk Away Harry, Knockbrack Rambler all hold-up types), Brave Endeavour can dictate terms without pressure through the early stages. The lack of pace pressure means prominent runners like Tropical Image and Derby Rock can track comfortably, while the hold-up horses will need the pace to collapse. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent runners who can position handily behind the leader without getting into an early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Brave Endeavour gets an easy lead and maintains stamina to 2f out
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows him to conserve energy for a genuine staying test, while the hold-up horses face too much ground to make up. His 9-year-old experience could prove crucial when others fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tropical Image or Derby Rock can sit second/third and pounce when Brave Endeavour weakens
scenarios.body: The patient prominent approach pays off as they avoid early exertion but stay close enough to capitalise. Tropical Image's course win gives her a key edge in this tactical battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the modest early pace sets up perfectly for Whispering Willow's hold-up style
scenarios.body: Her recent chase debut second at Downpatrick proves she can time her run correctly over fences. The slow tempo allows maximum time to organise her challenge from the back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse And Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses hit the front together in the final furlong after Brave Endeavour stops
scenarios.body: The weak pace creates a messy finish where stamina becomes secondary to who can quicken best. Class levels are so similar that any of the better-rated horses could prevail.

watchPoints.text: Brave Endeavour's jumping under pressure - he was tailed off when challenged on chase debut and may repeat errors if headed
Whispering Willow's positioning through the early stages - if she gets too far back in the small field she'll need the pace to collapse completely
Tropical Image's jumping rhythm early on - any mistakes will compromise her prominent position behind the likely uncontested leader
Derby Rock's fitness after 291 days off - any signs of blowing or struggling to keep up will end his chances quickly
The pace through the first circuit - if Brave Endeavour goes too fast early the hold-up horses come right into play

races.name: John J. Galvin Chase

runners_data.name: Blood Destiny
runners_data.note: Uncontested leader who won this race last year and handles good ground well, though 34 days off may leave him vulnerable late on
runners_data.comment: Has clear claims back at this level, even having to concede weight all round
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile ground-wise; won this last year and has since added a fourth chase win in a Grade 3 at Naas; ran second to Energumene in a Grade 2 in April before his no-show in a Grade 1 last time; has clear claims back at this level, even having to concede weight all round.

runners_data.name: Classic Getaway
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from the in-form Mullins yard who reads well in the context of this field despite not being at his absolute best recently
runners_data.comment: Not been at his best for a while but this is easier than he's accustomed to
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't been at his best since winning last year's Grade 2 Red Mills at Gowran but a couple of subsequent runs read well, especially in the context of today's easier assignment; unlikely to be far away; any rain welcomed.

runners_data.name: Jesse Evans
runners_data.note: Strong traveller who can sit handy and has excellent form on good ground, with recent 4-length defeat suggesting he's ready to strike
runners_data.comment: Beaten 4l in a 2m4f Grade 3 at Killarney three weeks ago and he's a player on these terms
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner who is 1-9 over fences, though was runner-up in last summer's Galway Plate; all the sharper for his comeback run when beaten 4l in a 2m4f Grade 3 at Killarney three weeks ago and he's a player on these terms.

runners_data.name: Eagle Fang
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing first-time visor who has been impressing in hurdle races but still learning his trade over fences
runners_data.comment: Excellent efforts in deep 3m handicap hurdles in recent weeks; has won over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Excellent efforts in deep 3m handicap hurdles in recent weeks, with the new visor working well; still early days over fences and the form he showed in winning at Thurles suggests he could be as effective in this discipline.

runners_data.name: Lisleigh Lad
runners_data.note: Handy hunter chase specialist with 7-pound claimer who will be outclassed at this graded level despite solid handicap form
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hunter chase winner who can hold his own in handicaps but unlikely to be overly competitive at this level.

runners_data.name: Itsalladream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from a yard with poor recent form who looks outgunned in this grade 3 company based on recent efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Has won a maiden hurdle and a novice chase; has looked a bit outclassed in Grade 3s in his last three races and a similar scenario seems likely in this company (well behind Jesse Evans last time).

races.paceDynamic: Blood Destiny will lead from the start with no obvious challengers for the front, setting a comfortable gallop in this small field of six. Classic Getaway, Jesse Evans, Eagle Fang and Lisleigh Lad will all settle in behind in a compressed pack, while Itsalladream may drop out the back. With no pace pressure on Blood Destiny, the race will develop into a tactical affair where the prominent runners can track the leader and time their challenges. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent runners who can position close enough to strike when the pace lifts, rather than hold-up horses who may struggle to make up ground in a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny maintains his rhythm and jumps fluently throughout the race
scenarios.body: The defending champion controls the tempo completely and has enough in reserve to repel late challenges, benefiting from the lack of early pace pressure. His class and course experience prove decisive when others struggle to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can position perfectly behind Blood Destiny and time their move
scenarios.body: Jesse Evans or Classic Getaway travel strongly in behind before launching a well-timed challenge at the second-last fence. The tactical nature of the race suits horses that can quicken from prominent positions rather than those coming from too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Leader Folds
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny's jumping deteriorates or the pace pressure tells on his 34-day break
scenarios.body: Classic Getaway or Jesse Evans inherit the lead and the race becomes a staying test between the prominent runners. Eagle Fang's stamina questions are exposed while the more experienced chasers battle it out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Back Marker
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the small field and Itsalladream gets a dream run
scenarios.body: The hold-up horse benefits from a crawling gallop and manages to pick up the pieces when the others come back to him. This requires perfect timing and the front-runners to stop quickly.

watchPoints.text: Blood Destiny's jumping fluency early on - any mistakes will invite pressure from the prominent runners tracking him
Jesse Evans and Classic Getaway positioning behind the leader - whoever gets the better stalking position holds a tactical advantage
Eagle Fang's response to the visor and whether his hurdle form translates to this superior level over fences
The pace through the first circuit - if it's genuinely slow it could bring Itsalladream into play unexpectedly
Classic Getaway's jumping - needs to be more fluent than recent efforts to mount a serious challenge

races.name: Beasley Engineering Hunters Chase

runners_data.name: Solitary Man
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who beat What Path by 1.5 lengths at Killarney three weeks ago and suits this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Has a particular fondness for Killarney and won for the fifth time there three weeks ago, where he beat What Path by 1.5l over a slightly shorter trip; was just doing enough, so headgear back on; likes good ground.

runners_data.name: Heartbreak Weather
runners_data.note: Prominent style but concerning fall record either side of point win, risky proposition
runners_data.comment: Keeping on in second when exiting two out in 2m4f hunter chase at Punchestown
runners_data.spotlight: Couple of falls either side of point win in March; keeping on in second on rules debut when exiting two out in 2m4f hunter chase at Punchestown.

runners_data.name: Hunt Away
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with useful point form but faces much tougher opposition than Cork maiden
runners_data.spotlight: Useful point-to-point form including three wins; narrowly beaten in 3m maiden hunter chase at Cork, but this is way tougher.

runners_data.name: In Excelsis Deo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with Grade 2 handicap win on CV, needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Grade 2 handicap over 2m4f a couple of years ago for Harry Fry before losing form; some good efforts in point-to-points, including recent win under this jockey; previously, was only around 7l off stablemate Solitary Man over 2m4f at Cork (disqualified, rider weighed in marginally light).

runners_data.name: Big Interest
runners_data.note: Prominent style but disappointing overall form since December 2024 Down Royal win
runners_data.spotlight: Looked a smart prospect when beating Its On The Line at Down Royal in December 2024; disappointing overall since then, except for an 18l Fairyhouse win last year; 66-1 at Punchestown festival, still prominent when exiting a mile out; well held in a point a week later.

runners_data.name: Call The Tune
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was only 2 lengths behind What Path in February banks contest
runners_data.spotlight: Useful soft-ground staying handicapper for Barry Connell back in the day; yet to win a point but only 2l off What Path in banks' contest in February; well held over the banks at Punchestown last month.

runners_data.name: Bartlemy Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who was second in this race last year after winning Killarney hunter chase debut
runners_data.spotlight: Good record in point-to-points, winning five; having won his first hunter chase start at Killarney, was favourite when second in this last year; well held in a couple of hunter chases this year and departed early on at Killarney.

runners_data.name: Five Star Getaway
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 12-year-old veteran was well beaten in Champion Hunter Chase
runners_data.spotlight: Old boy was smart handicapper in Britain back in the day; took advantage of his rivals' mishaps when winning at Fairyhouse; beaten a long way in the Champion Hunter Chase at Punchestown.

runners_data.name: Asphalt Cowboy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three wins at Downpatrick but trainer admits he's different horse there
runners_data.spotlight: All three hunter chase wins have come at Downpatrick, including a repeat of last year's victory in 3m5f contest just 10 days ago; trainer admits he's a different horse at that track, which renders him opposable here.

runners_data.name: What Path
runners_data.note: Front-runner revitalised by point-to-points with three spring wins, will control tempo
runners_data.spotlight: Useful 3m hurdler for Willie Mullins before fruitless spell over fences in Britain; seems to have been revitalised by point-to-points, winning three in the spring; in contention when slipping up in banks race at Punchestown; chased home Solitary Man at Killarney and 3lb better off here.

runners_data.name: Ambitious Fellow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with highest rating of 135 but jumping issues and maiden over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins over hurdles (rated 130), one of them here; maiden after 10 chase starts and has had jumping issues, but was second off 120 at Roscommon last summer; only beaten 7l in Champion Hunters Chase at Punchestown where he was a huge price.

races.paceDynamic: What Path will be the lone leader from flag to finish, having shown clear front-running tendencies and coming off strong spring form. With most rivals (Solitary Man, Hunt Away, Big Interest, Bartlemy Boy, Five Star Getaway) preferring prominent positions but unlikely to challenge What Path for outright lead, he'll get an uncontested gallop. The hold-up horses (In Excelsis Deo, Call The Tune, Asphalt Cowboy, Ambitious Fellow) will need the pace to collapse late over this staying trip. This tactical setup strongly favours the front-runner and prominent racers who can track the soft pace and kick when What Path weakens.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: What Path Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If What Path gets uncontested lead and maintains gallop
scenarios.body: His spring point-to-point wins show he's found form, and with no pace pressure he can dictate ideal fractions. Solitary Man and Hunt Away best placed to chase him home but may not peg him back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If What Path sets pace but weakens final furlong
scenarios.body: Solitary Man showed he can beat What Path at Killarney and is 1.5 lengths better on that form. His prominent style lets him track the leader and time his challenge perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If early pace is faster than expected creating collapse
scenarios.body: In Excelsis Deo and Ambitious Fellow have highest ratings and can benefit from strong gallop. Their hold-up styles become assets if front-runners go too hard early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or What Path stops suddenly
scenarios.body: Heartbreak Weather has falling history but showed ability when second at Punchestown. Hunt Away could benefit from reduced field if others make mistakes.

Solitary Man beaten What Path at Killarney recently and gets weight relief, making him key danger
In Excelsis Deo and Ambitious Fellow need strong early pace to bring hold-up style into play
Asphalt Cowboy won at Downpatrick 10 days ago but trainer says he's different horse there versus here

races.name: Bryan MacMahon (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race

runners_data.name: Minnatrix
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with highest rating (OR 117) but 80-1 odds on hurdle debut suggest connections lack confidence
runners_data.spotlight: Ran to a useful level when runner-up in a Roscommon bumper (good to yielding); surprisingly lengthy odds at 80-1 for his recent hurdle debut at Killarney where he was on the retreat when falling (in first-time hood); on that debut effort he commands respect.

runners_data.name: Thelittleballerina
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with 8-length win but 48 days since last run may blunt sharpness
runners_data.spotlight: Built on her pleasing debut to win on yielding ground at Clonmel (2m4f) by a comfortable 8l; didn't beat rubbish that day and, from the family of Bellshill, she looks a nice prospect.

runners_data.name: Gusserane
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity after pulling up in both point-to-points, lightly raced could be anything
runners_data.spotlight: Makes no appeal after pulling up in his two points.

runners_data.name: Echoes Of Jane
runners_data.note: Trainer won last two renewals of this race, hood added suggests yard expects improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Signs of ability in both her point runs and her yard has won the last two renewals of this bumper; hood added.

runners_data.name: Caman Hill
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 371-day absence but form has worked out well with placed horses progressing
runners_data.spotlight: Drew clear for a 9l success at Ballinrobe (good) last May and that form has worked out well, with both placed horses progressing to better things; the absence is worrying but he's clearly useful.

runners_data.name: The Boysofairhill
runners_data.note: Raced freely in recent bumper fifth, cheekpieces previously applied suggest temperament issues
runners_data.spotlight: Took five goes to win a point and only fifth of eight in last month's bumper, though he did race freely; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Cloonbonniffe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse beaten 11 lengths when weakening at Sligo, needs to find more here
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten about 11l at Sligo where he weakened when it mattered; has ability but needs more here.

runners_data.name: Martymill
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who hasn't matched debut fourth since, softer ground could help
runners_data.comment: Respected on the strength of his debut effort and rain would be welcomed
runners_data.spotlight: Not without hope on the strength of his debut run when fourth at Fairyhouse but unable to match that form since; however, getting back on softer ground could help (should it rain) and so too might cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: An Bhoireann
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but beaten 82 lengths and 25 lengths in bumpers, tongue tie added
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 82l and 25l in his two bumpers; now has tongue tied; couldn't recommend.

runners_data.name: Rusty Finure
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 520-day absence, previously beaten 60 lengths combined
runners_data.comment: Beaten a shade under 60l in bumpers here and at Limerick; the last was in late 2024
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten a shade under 60l in bumpers here and at Limerick; the last was in late 2024.

runners_data.name: Whatdoyoucallhim
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who fades in finish, tailed off in three bumpers and hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off in three bumpers and suffered the same fate on hurdle debut; cheekpieces tried.

races.paceDynamic: Thelittleballerina and Caman Hill are confirmed early leaders who will ensure a solid gallop from the start in this 11-runner field. Both have shown they can sustain their pace over this 2m4f trip, with Thelittleballerina's 8-length Clonmel win and Caman Hill's 9-length Ballinrobe success proving their front-running credentials. The pace will be genuine but not suicidal, creating a fair test for all running styles. This honest gallop will favour horses with proven stamina who can stay the trip strongly, benefiting prominent racers and hold-up horses with tactical speed over pure front-runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Grind
scenarios.trigger: If both Thelittleballerina and Caman Hill maintain their positions and set a steady tempo throughout
scenarios.body: The pace becomes a true stamina test where class and fitness tell in the final furlong. Minnatrix's hold-up style and superior rating (OR 117) plus Echoes Of Jane's yard record become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If one or both front-runners fade early leaving no clear pace-setter
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical with bunching occurring, suiting horses who can quicken off a slow pace. Martymill's prominent style and Cloonbonniffe's hold-up tactics work best in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Caman Hill Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Caman Hill's class tells and his 371-day absence proves irrelevant
scenarios.body: His 9-length Ballinrobe form that worked out well gives him the edge over less experienced rivals. Thelittleballerina's front-running keeps him honest but his superior form prevails.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too strong and established form proves unreliable
scenarios.body: Lightly-raced types with minimal exposure get first run on tiring favourites. Gusserane's unknown ability or The Boysofairhill's recent outing could spring surprises.

Thelittleballerina's early pace - if she goes too fast she'll compromise her finishing kick
Minnatrix's market support despite 80-1 hurdle debut odds - any money could indicate hidden ability
Echoes Of Jane's hood application - first-time headgear often signals trainer expects significant improvement
The Boysofairhill's settling early - previous free-running suggests he needs to relax to be competitive
